# OperantKitLog (OKL v1)

> Specification of OKL v1, a plain-text, tab-separated log format for operant and respondent conditioning sessions (responses, reinforcer start and end, state changes, phases), with a self-describing header and codebook, a formal EBNF grammar, and valid/invalid conformance fixtures.

OperantKitLog is part of OperantKit, a set of Python/Rust packages for designing and running operant and respondent conditioning experiments (reinforcement schedules, session recording, analysis). This repository contains the specification only; use it when you write a reader or writer for session logs in any language, instead of inventing a CSV or JSON layout.

## Example file

```text
# OKL v1
# session_name = "minimal"
# clock_type = "ManualClock"
# session_start = 0.0
# events:
#   response          : id:int operandum:int?
# ---
0.0	response	0	-
1.5	response	1	-
3.0	response	2	0
```

Header lines start with `#`; after `# ---` each line is `timestamp<TAB>event_type<TAB>columns...`, with `-` for an absent optional value.

## Implementations

```bash
pip install session-recorder   # Python writer (OklSink) and reader (read_log, iter_records)
```

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/README.md): contents, 30-second example, stability contract, conformance
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/AGENTS.md): when to use this specification and what not to do
- [Wire format](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/spec/wire-format.md): file structure, escaping, stability contract
- [Header](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/spec/header.md) and [codebook](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/spec/codebook.md): required fields and canonical event types
- [Grammar](https://github.com/OperantKit/OperantKitLog/blob/main/spec/grammar.ebnf): formal EBNF

## Related packages

- [session-recorder](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-recorder): Python implementation, tested against the conformance fixtures
- [session-analyzer](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-analyzer): analyses that read OKL v1 logs (`pip install session-analyzer`)
- [session-runner](https://github.com/OperantKit/session-runner): runs sessions whose events are written as OKL v1 (`pip install session-runner`)
